title: Private Deploy: observability tap with adaptive scrubbers and replay checkpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight observability tap for Private/Dedicated deployments that sits in front of existing collectors and provides: (1) tenant-aware adaptive scrubbing (PII redaction and policy-driven field removal), (2) replay-safe checkpointing to durable local storage for guaranteed delivery under backpressure, and (3) tracing hooks for KV cache hit/miss, model-routing decisions, and request latency propagation. Goal is to reduce cross-tenant leakage risk, retain bounded-delivery guarantees for on-prem customers, and surface latency/error signals to per-tenant dashboards without adding undue CPU/memory pressure to customer clusters.

Design highlights: The tap is a single-process binary (go) deployed as a DaemonSet or sidecar depending on topology. It intercepts telemetry via a transparent TCP/HTTP capture (prefix agent) and forks streams to: (A) local durability store (leveldb+segment files) for checkpoints, (B) a scrub pipeline that applies JSONPath-based policy rules fetched from the control plane, and (C) the upstream collector (with optional sampling hints). Checkpoints are time-windowed (default 5m segments) and retention/size limits are configurable per-tenant. Scrubber policies support allowlists, blocklists, regex redact, and field-preserve masks; policies are versioned to allow safe roll-forward and rollback.

Tracing hooks: We will emit deterministic trace annotations for the following events: tap.ingest, tap.scrub.start, tap.scrub.redact(<field>), tap.checkpoint.write, tap.forward.outbound, runtime.kv.cache.hit/miss, routing.model.variant.select. Traces include a tenant-scoped trace_id and use opaque tenant IDs (no raw customer identifiers).

Backpressure and Replay: When the upstream collector is slow, the tap will backpressure locally and write to the checkpoint store. A bounded in-memory queue + persistent segment fallback ensures no unbounded memory growth. A replay worker guarantees at-least-once delivery to upstream with idempotency hints. Checkpoint metrics expose segment_age_seconds and replay_lag_seconds to drive alerts.

Dashboards & Alerts: New Grafana dashboards per-tenant and aggregate: ingress-throughput, scrub-redaction-rate, checkpoint-store-size, replay-lag, per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, per-route error-rate, and model-variant error breakdown. Alert rules: replay_lag_seconds > 300 => paging P1 for dedicated customers; scrub-redaction-rate spike (>5x baseline) => Investigate sudden PII leakage.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Tap handles 10k/s avg telemetry flow on t3.medium-equivalent on-prem node with <5% CPU overhead vs baseline collector; (2) Policies can be updated from control plane and take effect within 30s without dropping data; (3) Checkpoint replay recovers 99.9% of messages within 1 hour under simulated upstream outage; (4) Tracing hooks are instrumented in runtime and surfaced in per-tenant traces / latency dashboards.

Rollout plan: 1) dev build + unit/integration tests; 2) internal dogfood on staging private clusters for 2 weeks; 3) canary rollout to 3 small Private customers behind feature flag; 4) enable on larger Dedicated pools after metrics confirm latency and storage SLOs.

Operational considerations & trade-offs: - Privacy vs usability: aggressive scrubbing reduces telemetry fidelity; plan to provide sampling + structured-trace-hints to preserve high-level SLO monitoring while redacting sensitive fields. - Storage cost: checkpoint retention configurable per-tenant; recommend default 24h for Private deployments. - Complexity: policy evaluation must be fast and safe; avoid full JS runtime in hot path.
tasks: Implement tap binary and config loader
Implement policy-fetch and local cache with versioning
Implement persistent checkpoint store with segmenting and GC
Add tracing annotations and wire to runtime instrumentation
Add replay worker with idempotency hints and backoff
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules
E2E test harness: upstream outage + replay correctness
Docs: operator install, feature flags, policy examples
comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Chen: Initial PRD posted to Confluence (link below). Primary ask from enterprise customers: guarantee no PII can escape private clusters; want per-tenant latency SLOs regardless of scrub rules.
2026-02-25 - Daniel Ortiz: Prototype of checkpoint store completed. Observed stable writes at 12k/s on our CI nodes. Need to add index compaction for long-running nodes.

2026-02-28 - Priya Nair (Security): Please ensure scrub policy changes are auditable and signed. We'll require KMS-backed signatures for policy pushes in Private. Marking security_review_required=true.
2026-03-03 - SRE Lead (Jonas Miller): Replay worker must expose metrics for per-tenant replay success/failure counts. Also propose a soft quota to avoid single tenant filling node disk.
2026-03-07 - Daniel Ortiz: Added backoff + disk quota enforcement. Updated acceptance tests to include quota exhaustion scenario.
notes: This ticket surfaces both infra work and sensitive security requirements. Coordinate closely with Security, SRE, and Solutions Engineering for customer-specific policy templates.
implementation_decisions: Language: Go for low-latency binary and small distro footprint
Checkpoint format: append-only segment files + compacted index for replay
Policy DSL: JSONPath + regex with control-plane versioning (no arbitrary code execution)
